items.title: Finishing a workout cancels the pending rest-timer push
steps: Start a session. Log the LAST set of the workout while the rest timer is still counting down.
Immediately finish/complete the workout before the rest timer reaches 0.
Verify you do NOT receive a 'Rest over - time for your next set' push afterwards (there is no next set).
Sanity: log a non-last set, let the rest timer run out normally, and verify the rest push STILL fires as before.
items.notes: [2026-06-08] @maaiz: 'I finished a workout after entering the last set before the rest timer was finished but I still got the rest timer push which is useless'. The countdown's finish() (beep + REST_DONE push) kept firing because doSaveWorkout didn't cancel the running rest timer. Fix: call rest.stop() at the top of the workout-complete path - stop() clears the interval so finish() never runs, suppressing the push. Normal rest-end pushes (non-final sets) are unaffected. (qa: session-finish-cancels-rest-push)

items.title: Admins get a push + system-notification when any other user submits a bug / idea / feedback / retest
items.introducedBy: @maaiz report 'Admins aren't getting qa comments or bugs or idea submissions by other users'
steps: As a non-admin user (and with push enabled on a separate admin device), submit a bug via the in-app QA panel. Verify each ADMIN receives a push notification titled like '🐞 New bug report from <username>' with the report text as the body, and tapping it deep-links to /qa focused on the item.

As a NON-admin, open the system feed. Verify NO other-user submissions appear (the /api/qa/comments/admin-feed endpoint returns nothing for non-admins).
items.notes:
[2026-06-08] LEAK FIX. @maaiz: a QA submission pushed to Amanii's logged-OUT phone 'like she was an admin'. Cause: push is device-bound - sendPushToUser(adminId) hits every PushSubscription row under an admin's userId, and a row is only removed when the user taps Log out (doLogout -> DELETE /api/push/subscribe). An admin who logged in on her phone and ended the session WITHOUT logging out left a stale {userId:admin, endpoint:herPhone} row, so admin pushes kept landing there. Fix: (a) DELETE /api/push/subscribe no longer requires a session - deletes by endpoint alone so a logged-out device can purge a stale row; (b) on app load with no session the client unsubscribes + DELETEs this device's subscription; (c) the mount effect no longer auto-subscribes a possibly-logged-out device. Recipient query (role=admin OR extraRoles has admin) was already correct. (qa: admin-submission-notifications)

[2026-06-05 <sha7>] Per @maaiz 'I want admins to always get a push notification and see the submission in system notifications when someone submits anything except themselves'. Three pieces: (1) POST /api/qa/comment now finds every admin (role==='admin' OR extraRoles has 'admin'), excludes the submitter, and awaits sendPushToUser for each with a type-aware title (🐞/💡/📝/🔄) + note snippet + deep-link; awaited like the repo mirror so Vercel doesn't kill the function early. (2) New GET /api/qa/comments/admin-feed returns the last 30d / 50 most-recent QAComments from OTHERS (includes anonymous userId=null; excludes the admin's own) enriched with submitter username; returns [] for non-admins so the client can call it unconditionally. (3) lib/systemNotifications.ts fetchAdminSubmissionNotifications + ack tracking (ironlog-admin-sub-acks-v1); page.tsx merges them into the systemNotifs feed as a third bubble kind alongside bundled + patch notifs, with matching unread snapshot/scroll/badge wiring. Admin-only surface reusing the existing system feed — no new route, so no TUTORIAL_STEPS entry. Note: push delivery still requires the admin to have granted notification permission (existing PushSubscription infra); the in-app feed is the always-on fallback.

The patch number was frozen at v1.2.14 because app/api/version/route.ts counted only PATCHLOG headers matching /^## (QA pass|Feature|Fix|Polish)/, but the header vocabulary had drifted (## Feat x23, ## Bugfix x5, ## Chore, ## Hotfix don't match), so several deploys didn't move the count (156). Documented the mechanic in CLAUDE.md. The update PROMPT itself was fine (SHA-based) - the banner only shows when the app is open across a deploy; a cold PWA start gets the green 'UPDATED TO v' toast, which previously showed the unchanged 1.2.14. This commit adds one new section so the live count becomes 143; appVersion = '1.2.' + max(0, 143 - 142) = '1.2.1'. Also bumped package.json version to 1.2.0 to keep tooling in sync. items.title: Auto-update banner + post-update toast actually render (moved into HomeGlobals' overlay-portal root)
items.introducedBy: @maaiz report — 'Not getting any banner to refresh the app'
steps: On home (or any normal view), after a fresh deploy + a focus/visibility event (or wait 5 min), verify the cyan banner '🔄 NEW VERSION AVAILABLE · v<X>' slides in at the top with REFRESH + × buttons.
Tap REFRESH. Verify the page reloads via cache-bust URL navigation and lands on the new bundle. After load, the green '✓ UPDATED TO v<X>' toast appears for ~4.5 s, then auto-dismisses.
Same flow from Messages, Progress, Ranks, Groups, Friends, Clients — verify the banner is visible on every view (previously only the unreachable fall-through return rendered it).
Start a workout session. While `started === true`, verify NEITHER banner NOR toast renders (suppressed via `updateOverlayDisabled={started}` passed to HomeGlobals).
Dismiss the banner via ×. Verify the dismissal sticks across the current SHA but a fresh deploy resurfaces it on the next focus/poll.
items.notes:
[2026-06-08] STALE-BUNDLE FIX. @maaiz: a deploy 'didn't prompt to update, had to force close to make updates live'. runningSha was read from /api/version (the SERVER's current SHA) on mount, not the SHA of the loaded bundle - so a stale iOS PWA bundle set runningSha=latestSha=server and the banner never fired (the card even showed the new version while running old code). Fix: next.config.js bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_SHA + NEXT_PUBLIC_BUILD_VERSION into the bundle; runningSha now comes from the baked value (real loaded build) while latestSha stays from /api/version, so when the server is ahead the cyan banner fires reliably (one tap REFRESH, no force-close). Green 'UPDATED TO v' toast now keys off the baked SHA changing. Dev falls back to old behaviour. (qa: app-update-overlay-cross-view)

[2026-05-27 <sha7>] Root cause: the original implementation in PR #7 put the banner JSX in HomePage's main fall-through return (~line 19650). HomePage has multiple `if (view === ...) return (...)` early returns for home / messages / conversation / workout etc — every one of them bypasses the main return. The banner JSX literally never reached the DOM for any normal view. Fix: extracted a self-contained `AppUpdateOverlay` component (top-level, manages its own /api/version state + focus/visibility/interval listeners) and mounted it inside `HomeGlobals` which renders to a SEPARATE React root via the overlay portal (`overlayRootRef`) — that root is independent of every view's early return, so the overlay renders unconditionally. HomeGlobals now takes a `updateOverlayDisabled` prop (wired to HomePage's `started` flag) so the banner stays hidden during an active workout. Dead state + JSX in HomePage removed. Source: @maaiz 'Not getting any banner to refresh the app' after multiple deploys.

items.title: Home bottom nav is portaled to document.body so it's truly fixed to the viewport (not floating mid-page on scroll)
steps: Open the home view. Verify the floating bottom hub (Messages / Progress / Ranks / Groups / Friends / Clients) sits at the bottom of the viewport.

Scroll down to the bottom of the home content (past Day 5, SAVED ROUTINES, MY EXERCISES). Verify the bottom hub STAYS at the bottom of the visible screen — it does not appear above SAVED ROUTINES or anywhere else in the page flow.
Scroll back to the top of the home view. Hub remains at the bottom of the viewport.
Switch to another view (e.g. Ranks). Verify the home hub no longer appears (it's only rendered while view === 'home').
Confirm the home spacer above the hub still preserves bottom padding so the last card isn't covered when scrolled all the way down.
items.notes: [2026-05-27 <sha7>] Root cause: the home view JSX is wrapped in AnimatePresence > motion.div with an x/opacity transform animation. Transformed ancestors create a containing block for descendants with `position: fixed` — the nav (zIndex 60, `position: fixed; bottom: 0`) was anchored to the motion.div's bottom edge, NOT the viewport. With the motion.div taller than 100dvh (home content extends past the viewport), the nav floated wherever the bottom of the motion.div was — i.e., somewhere mid-content. Fix: wrap the nav block in `createPortal(..., document.body)` so it renders directly under document.body, escaping every transformed ancestor. `position: fixed` then anchors to the viewport as intended. Source: @maaiz screenshot showing nav appearing above SAVED ROUTINES section + 'Might be more wrong with the bottom tabs, I think they should be fixed at the bottom with everything else scrolling'.

items.title: Group chat no longer pulls back to the bottom of history when the user scrolls up
steps: Open a group chat with enough messages to scroll. Drag UP to view older messages — verify the chat stays put at the scroll position you reached (no auto-pull back to the bottom).
While scrolled up, wait through one or two poll cycles (~5 s each). Verify your scroll position is preserved across polls; new messages arriving below should NOT yank you down.
Scroll back to the bottom. Verify a new incoming message auto-scrolls (within 150 px of bottom = nearBottom = true).
Close the group chat and reopen. Verify it lands at the bottom (initial mount pin still works).
items.notes: [2026-05-27 <sha7>] Root cause: the group chat's scroll container used an INLINE ref callback `(el) => { ref.current = el; if (el) el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight }`. Inline callbacks get a new function reference every render, so React re-runs the cleanup/setup cycle and the `scrollTop = scrollHeight` line fired on EVERY render — every poll, every new message, every prop change destroyed the user's scroll position. Fix: stable `ref={groupChatScrollRef}` + a dedicated useEffect mirroring the DM convo pattern (lines ~7146): initial mount pin (one-shot, via groupChatInitialPinRef), then nearBottom-aware auto-scroll on subsequent message updates (within 150 px of bottom = auto-scroll, else respect user's position). Source: @maaiz 'On chat logs I'm still getting pulled to the bottom of the chat history if I scroll up, it's not letting me actually scroll to where I want'.

items.title: DM message send requires accepted friendship OR trainer-client link (system messages bypass)
steps: Open a DM conversation with a user you are NOT friends with and NOT in a trainer-client relationship with. Try to send a text message. Verify the API returns 403 with the message 'You can only message friends or your trainer/client. Send a friend request first.'
Add the user as a friend (POST then accept). Send a text message again. Verify it goes through (200).
Remove the friendship. Try to send a text message. Verify it fails again with 403.
Set up a trainer-client relationship (adoption + accept). Verify the trainer can DM the client and vice versa even without a friendship — trainer-client link satisfies the gate.
Send a system-typed message (e.g. friend_request, adoption_request) from another endpoint. Verify it lands regardless of relationship — system types bypass the gate.
items.notes: [2026-06-03 <sha7>] Per @maaiz 'Make users unable to message each other if not friends or client and trainer'. POST /api/messages for `type === "text"` now does a Promise.all of (a) accepted Friendship in either direction, (b) TrainerClient where viewer=trainer, (c) TrainerClient where viewer=client. If all three return null → 403 with friendly copy. System types (friend_request, friend_accepted, adoption_request, adoption_accepted, adoption_declined, plan_proposal, etc) bypass the gate because they're created via prisma.message.create directly from other route handlers (/api/friends, /api/trainer/request, etc), not through this POST. The bootstrap flow (sending a friend request to a stranger to BECOME their friend) still works. Slice 1/N — UI-side gating (hide the input field when no relationship) is a follow-up; this slice is the defensive server-side enforcement.

items.title: Friend request bubble pill shows CANCELLED vs DECLINED instead of catch-all RESOLVED
steps: Send a friend request to a user. Verify the bubble shows PENDING.
From the sender side, cancel (× button). Verify the bubble pill flips to CANCELLED (neutral grey) — not the old RESOLVED catch-all.
Send another friend request to the same user. Verify the previously-cancelled row is REUSED (no orphan friendship records, no duplicate bubbles in the thread).
From the recipient side, decline a pending request. Verify the bubble pill flips to DECLINED (red).
Send a friend request again to that same user. Verify the previously-declined row is REUSED — sides swap so the new requester is userAId.
Accept a friend request as the recipient. Verify pill shows ACCEPTED.
Historic rows that were hard-deleted before this change (legacy cancelled/declined) — verify the bubble still falls back to RESOLVED so the user thread doesn't break.
items.notes:
[2026-06-03 <sha7>] Per @maaiz 'Instead of resolved it can say friend request cancelled'. RESOLVED was the catch-all pill rendered when requestStatus came back null (because cancel and decline both hard-deleted the Friendship row). Fix:
• DELETE /api/friends — for pending status, set status='cancelled' (audit-preserving). For accepted, still hard-delete (unfriend semantic).
• PATCH /api/friends action='decline' — set status='declined' instead of deleting.
• POST /api/friends against an existing cancelled or declined row — re-issue: bump status back to pending, swap sides so caller becomes userAId, refresh requestedAt, re-emit the friend_request message + push.
• Pill render — added explicit CANCELLED (neutral) and DECLINED (red) labels; RESOLVED kept only as legacy fallback when requestStatus is null (pre-soft-delete rows).
No schema migration — status is a plain string. /api/messages/[userId] GET already joined Friendship.status into the message via requestId so the pill labels switched automatically once the API stopped hard-deleting.

Open Settings → 💡 EXTRA BRIGHT card. Verify the copy reads 'The baseline already lifts contrast for gym-readability. Toggle ON for an EVEN stronger boost (brighter fonts, deeper backgrounds) when your phone is dimmed to near-minimum.'

Replaced the conditional `{brightText && <style>filter: brightness(1.16)...</style>}` with an unconditional `<style>` that always emits a CSS filter — the OFF state now uses the previous ON values (`brightness(1.16) contrast(1.06) saturate(1.05)`) as the baseline, and the ON state bumps to `brightness(1.30) contrast(1.15) saturate(1.05)`. items.title: Profile preview modal actually opens from every view (was unreachable on early-return view branches)

items.notes: [2026-06-03 <sha7>] Root cause @maaiz reported with 3 screenshots ('Nothing happens when clicking username on any of these leaderboards and rankings'): the ProfilePreviewModal was mounted in HomePage's main fall-through return. View branches that use `return (...)` short-circuits — friendsHub (line 13095), globalLeaderboard (line 13076), clientsHub, etc — bypass that main return entirely, so the modal was never rendered into the DOM on those views. setPreviewUserId(uid) triggered a re-render but the modal mount was unreachable, so nothing visible happened. Same architectural class as the auto-update banner regression. Fix: extended HomeGlobals (which renders into a separate React root via overlayRootRef and is therefore reachable from every view) with new optional props — previewUserId, onClosePreview, onPreviewOpenDM, onPreviewFriendshipChanged, viewer, tierThemeForPreview — and moved the modal mount inside it. HomePage passes the state + callbacks through; the dead mount on HomePage's main return is removed. The DM conversation path worked previously only because that view uses `_content =` (assignment) instead of `return`, so it still reached the main return — but that's brittle; routing through HomeGlobals unifies the path.

items.title: QA patch notifications fire OS push (not just in-app system feed)
steps: After a QA pass deploys, run `curl -X POST https://<host>/api/admin/qa-push-fanout -H 'x-admin-key: $ADMIN_SECRET' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"since":"<pass-timestamp ISO>"}'`.
Endpoint returns `{ sent, total, sinceUsed, candidates }`. Verify `sent` matches the number of unique users whose comments were processed in the pass.

On a phone subscribed to push for an affected user, verify an OS-level notification appears with title '🔧 IRONLOG · Patch shipped' and the simplified summary as body. Tap → deep-links to /qa?focus=<itemId>#comment-<id>.
Run the endpoint a second time with the same `since`. Verify `sent: 0` (pushedAt is now set on every comment, so the duplicate-guard fires).
Sanity: a user with no PushSubscription rows silently no-ops — `sendPushToUser` already catches that path. The pushedAt timestamp is still set so we don't keep retrying.
items.notes: [2026-06-03 <sha7>] @maaiz reported 'maaiz did not get push notification of the patches, but it's in his system messages log'. Investigation: sendPushToUser is wired for friend requests / trainer requests / DMs / trainer proposals but NEVER for qa-processed.json updates. The IRONLOG SYSTEM feed bubble was the ONLY surface — push for processed patches was simply never built (earlier session-summary claims about push firing were wrong). Fix: added a `pushedAt DateTime?` field to QAComment (indexed on (userId, pushedAt)) + a new admin endpoint POST /api/admin/qa-push-fanout that reads qa-processed.json, finds in-window unpushed comments owned by a user, fires sendPushToUser with the simplified summary as the push body, and stamps pushedAt to prevent duplicates. Time-windowed via the `since` body param (defaults to NOW - 1 h) so the 180 historic comments don't blast as a one-time storm — only entries newer than `since` are pushed. I call the endpoint manually after each QA pass push. For the 2026-06-03 pass itself: 6 comments processed across @maaiz / @azim / @humaam; expected `sent` = number of users with active PushSubscription rows for those user ids. Slice 1/N — next slice would automate the curl call from the deploy webhook so the human doesn't have to remember; cron-on-Vercel could also poll and fanout.

steps: Open a DM thread with multiple messages. Scroll so the most recent incoming message is at the BOTTOM of the screen.

Tap the avatar/@username chip on that bottom-of-screen message. Verify the profile preview modal opens with the headline (big avatar + tier badge + username + joined date) FULLY visible — not scrolled past to the action buttons.

items.notes: [2026-06-03 <sha7>] Round 2: the first useEffect+RAF fix didn't stick. @maaiz reported the modal STILL opens scrolled past the headline after the v1.2.9 deploy. Switched to `useLayoutEffect` with deps `[userId, loading]` so the scroll-reset fires synchronously after DOM mutations and BEFORE the browser paints — re-runs on initial mount AND when `loading` flips false (i.e. content height grows after the data fetch, which is when iOS's scroll-into-view was racing our reset). Both useEffect+RAF and useLayoutEffect approaches are kept in the file for forensic reference; the layout-effect on data-load is the operative one.\n\n[2026-06-03 <sha7>] @maaiz reported 'When opening profile view from inside a chatlog, misalignment issues' with a screenshot showing the modal opened with ONLY the action buttons (MESSAGE / REMOVE FRIEND / YOUR CLIENT / DISOWN CLIENT) visible — the headline (avatar + tier + username + joined date) was scrolled past the top of the modal. Root cause: the inner panel has overflowY:auto (bounded by maxHeight: calc(100dvh - 48px) so it never extends past the safe area) and on iOS the panel was auto-scrolling toward the originally-focused element from the chat — a tap point near the bottom of the screen pulls the panel's scroll position down too. First-attempt fix: added an `innerPanelRef` to the inner panel + a `requestAnimationFrame` in the body-scroll-lock useEffect that sets `scrollTop = 0` after one paint. The RAF defer was meant to dodge iOS's own scroll-into-view but didn't — see round 2 above.

steps: Open a profile preview from any entry point. Verify the modal sits centered on the viewport with the backdrop blur over the entire page.

If the modal content is taller than the viewport (rare — happens at large dynamic type), the INNER panel scrolls internally with native momentum, capped at calc(100dvh - 48px) so it never extends past the safe area.

items.notes: [2026-05-27 <sha7>] User report (with screenshot showing modal anchored to bottom of viewport + visible scrollbar): 'Shouldn't be any scroll when viewing profile'. Two-part fix: (1) `useEffect` inside ProfilePreviewModal sets `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` on mount and restores on unmount — kills any body-scroll-through during the modal lifetime. (2) Inner panel gains `maxHeight: calc(100dvh - 48px)` + `overflowY: auto` + `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch` + `overscroll-behavior: contain` so any overflow is bounded to the panel itself with native iOS momentum, instead of letting the page scroll behind it.

items.notes: [2026-05-27 <sha7>] The pro tip expanded modal sat at flex-end with `padding: '20px 22px 28px'` but no marginBottom. Even with zIndex 9600, the floating bottom hub (zIndex 60, but in the same motion.div stacking context with `position: fixed; bottom: 0`) sat on TOP visually and obscured the bottom ~96 px of the panel — last line of the tip + the HIDE buttons. Fix: `marginBottom: calc(96px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` lifts the panel above the hub, plus `maxHeight: calc(100dvh - 96px - safe-area - 24px)` + `overflowY: auto` ensures the panel itself contains its scroll if a tip ever exceeds the visible budget. Reported by @maaiz: 'Still can't read the Pro tips because the bottom buttons overlay them'.

items.title: Pull-to-refresh requires a deliberate drag — no longer fires when scrolling up in a short chat
steps: Open a short DM thread (one with few enough messages that the entire history fits without scrolling). Swipe upward (i.e. drag finger downward) as if to scroll up. Verify NO pull-to-refresh indicator appears and the chat does NOT refresh.
Same thread: scroll inside the chat normally — any momentum-scroll past the top of the visible area should NOT engage pull-to-refresh.

Same thread: from a paused state at the top, deliberately drag downward at least ~150 px. Verify the indicator appears and rotates, and on release the refresh fires (existing behaviour for an intentional pull).
Open a long DM thread. Scroll down to the middle, then drag downward to scroll up to the top. Verify reaching the top via scroll momentum does NOT trigger refresh.
Same flow on Group Chat (`groupChatPtr`) and the Messages inbox (`inboxPtr`). All three usePullToRefresh consumers share the hook so the fix applies everywhere.
items.notes:
[2026-05-27 <sha7>] usePullToRefresh (app/page.tsx ~line 3906) armed the gesture whenever a touch started with scrollTop ≤ 2 and began accumulating pullDistance the moment dy went positive. In a short chat where scrollTop is already 0, a normal upward-scroll gesture (which on iOS is a downward finger drag) immediately accumulated pull and could cross the 64-px threshold on release. Two-part fix:
• ARM_THRESHOLD = 30: a dead zone the finger must traverse downward before any indicator is shown. The first ~30 px of drag are treated as scroll/braking momentum, not pull intent. Visible distance is now `(dy - 30) × 0.5`, capped at 110.
• Cancellation: if dy ever goes negative (the user scrolled up at any point during the gesture), the gesture is permanently disqualified until the next touch. Reaching the top via momentum and bouncing back can no longer fire refresh.
Net effect: raw finger drag to trigger refresh went from 128 px (= 64/0.5) to 158 px (= 30 + 64/0.5) and must be a clean downward drag from rest. Refresh on intentional pull still works exactly as before. Source: @maaiz 'When I scroll up in a chatlog if it's too short or if I reach the top too quickly, it makes the chatlog refresh. The pull down to refresh feature needs to be more intentional, not accidental.'

items.title: Auto-banner prompts the user to refresh when a new deploy lands while their tab/PWA is open
items.introducedBy: @maaiz follow-up to form-cue regression report (munchy on stale bundle)
steps: Open the app, wait for it to finish loading (the running SHA is snapshot on mount via /api/version).

Deploy a new commit. Bring the app tab back to the foreground (or wait for the 5-min interval). Verify a cyan banner slides in at the top: '🔄 NEW VERSION AVAILABLE · v<version> · Refresh for the latest fixes.' with REFRESH + × buttons.
Tap REFRESH. Verify the page navigates (with a cache-bust query param) and reloads onto the new SHA. After load, banner is gone and Settings → APP VERSION shows the new running SHA.
Repeat the deploy scenario but tap × (dismiss). Verify the banner disappears and DOES NOT reappear on focus / interval poll. The dismissed SHA is stored in localStorage `ironlog.updateDismissedSha`.
Push ANOTHER deploy. Reopen / focus. Verify the banner resurfaces — because the new SHA differs from the dismissed one, dismissal doesn't carry over.

Start a workout session (tap a day card → START). While the session is active, push a deploy and bring the app forward. Verify NO banner is rendered (suppressed by `!started` guard) — set logging stays uninterrupted.
End the workout. Verify the banner now shows on the post-session view.
Settings → APP VERSION → CHECK FOR UPDATES still works as before (manual path unchanged).
items.notes: [2026-05-27 <sha7>] Settings already had a VersionCheckCard (lines ~3330) that snapshots the SHA on mount and offers a manual 'Check for updates' tap + SW SKIP_WAITING + cache-bust reload. The manual path required the user to dig into Settings — testers reporting already-fixed bugs (e.g. munchy on the form-cue regression after the longest-match fix landed) often hadn't refreshed. This wakes the existing flow up: snapshots runningSha on mount, re-polls /api/version on focus / visibilitychange / 5-min interval; when the server SHA differs from the running SHA AND it hasn't been dismissed, a cyan top banner appears with REFRESH + × buttons. Refresh reuses the same SW SKIP_WAITING + cache-bust URL navigation as Settings. Dismissal is per-SHA (localStorage `ironlog.updateDismissedSha`) so the next real deploy resurfaces it. Suppressed while `started === true` so it can't break mid-set logging. Source: @maaiz 'check if there's a way to force app reopens or refreshes on client side if there was a major update deployed like with the form cue for hanging leg raises shown wrong, munchy reported it but maybe he hasn't refreshed the app'.

steps: Create a brand-new account, log one workout. Open Progress → YOUR RANK. Verify Strength sub-rank score ≈ round(50 × 1/9) ≈ 6 (not 50), and the detail string ends with '· ramping 11%'. Verify Progression sub-rank similarly ramps (score ≈ 6, detail says 'X/9 weeks logged · ramping NN%').

Verify Lion-tier (T4) avatars are LOCKED (silhouetted), only Big Dawg-and-below avatars remain unlocked. If their selected avatar was a Lion one, verify it reverts to the default circle (no broken state).

Recalibration cleanup — toast re-fires after re-earning: with localStorage `ironlog.lastObservedTier.<uid>` initially at 4 (Lion) and current canonical at 3 (Big Dawg), reopen the app. Verify NO toast fires (silent demotion) BUT the key is bumped down to 3. Then bump the canonical tier back up to 4 (add more sessions, hit Lion again) → verify the LION toast fires when the next refresh lands.

Recalibration cleanup — milestone relock: verify the localStorage MILESTONE_STORAGE_KEY set no longer contains `tier-tiger` (Lion milestone) when current tier drops below 4. Log a workout that pushes you back to Lion → verify the Lion milestone celebration fires from the session-complete pipeline.
items.notes:
[2026-05-27 <sha7>] Replaces the flat-50 freebie on Strength + Progression for users with <9 training weeks. The flat floor pushed 13-day-old accounts to Lion off ~10 free headline points (Str 20% * 50 + Prog 12% * 50 - what they'd actually earn). New formula: rampFactor = min(1, weeklyVolumes.length / 9), score *= rampFactor. Applied to all three return paths in strengthSubRank (qualified=0, !hasData, full blend) and the <9-week return in progressionSubRank. Weeks measured as training weeks (weeklyVolumes.length, last 180d) not calendar weeks — prevents the 'dormant 9 weeks then suddenly Lion' loophole. Established users (≥9 weeks) unaffected. Detail strings get a '· ramping NN%' suffix while in ramp. Per @maaiz: 'Progression calculation can be used at stepped % every week until reaching 100 … Week 1 = 10% x normal calculation, Week 2 = 20% … not sure what your recommendation for strength is but could be similar.'

[2026-05-27 <sha7>] Recalibration cleanup (per @maaiz 'make sure all users are in their right tier, don't have additional tier avatars unlocked, and also make sure they get celebration for tier progressions'):
• `/api/avatars` GET now revokes tier-source UserAvatarUnlock rows where avatar.tier > current canonical tier, and clears the user's equipped avatarId if it's a now-relocked tier avatar. Lucky-source unlocks are never revoked.
• Tier promotion toast effect (app/page.tsx) re-enables the QUIET DEMOTION write that was disabled in the 2026-05-24 fix. Safe now under the serverCanonicalTier guard added in tier-promotion-toast — DB-truth, not transient initial-render. Without this, users whose localStorage `ironlog.lastObservedTier` was previously set to 4 (Lion) from the now-removed freebie can never trigger the Lion celebration when they legitimately earn it under the new ramp.
• Same demotion branch also relocks tier milestones (`tier-tiger` / `tier-lion` / `tier-gorilla` etc) in the client-side MILESTONE_STORAGE_KEY set when current tier drops below the milestone's required tier. Re-fires on the next session-save when the milestone is earned again.

items.title: Daily quest — extended pool + rotation + celebration animation + tier-point reward + leaderboard weighting
steps: (Planning slice — NO code shipped yet.) Read this notes block for the design.
Verify the quest chip auto-DISAPPEARS once completed + the celebration animation fires (NOT just turn green and stay).

items.notes:
[2026-05-23] Slice 1 shipped (pool expansion + per-user rotation):
- QUEST_POOL grew from 7 → 14 quests. New entries: Variety (3+ distinct exercises today), Volume push (15+ sets), Superset day, Drop set day, Get cardio in, Warmup pro (all warmups marked ✓), Tracker check (log weight/BF today).
- pickTodayQuest now takes optional `userId` and uses `hash(userId + iso)` for per-user random rotation. Same user sees a stable quest each day; different users see different quests on the same day. Falls back to anon-deterministic when no userId.
- QuestState extended with 8 optional new fields for the new quest criteria; home view computes them while walking today's history (distinct exercises, working set count, drop-set + cardio + superset detection, warmup-perfect, body-metric-today).
Slices NOT in this push: celebration animation + auto-dismiss when done; tier-score bonus per quest (cap +20); leaderboard weighting via canonical score.
[2026-05-23] Planning. Per @maaiz: (i) quest disappears + celebration on complete, (ii) extend pool, (iii) rotate randomly, (iv) award tier points, (v) somehow weigh on leaderboard progress.

Design sketch:
- Pool expansion (7 → 20-ish): add `q-distinct-3` (3+ exercises today), `q-superset` (a superset today), `q-dropset` (a drop set today), `q-cardio` (a cardio set today), `q-warmup-perfect` (mark all warmups ✓ today), `q-cooldown-perfect`, `q-body-metric` (log weight or BF today), `q-15-sets` (15+ working sets), `q-90min` (a session ≥ 90 min today), `q-share` (share a routine), `q-new-exercise` (try a new exercise today), `q-rpe-10` (one set at RPE 10 today).
- Rotation: deterministic per-user-per-day using `hash(userId + iso)` so different users see different quests, but the same user sees a stable quest each day. Stops day-rolling-over from flipping the quest mid-session.
- Celebration: small confetti burst + the chip fades out after 2.5s. Reuses the existing PB celebration overlay primitives (lib/celebrate ?) or framer-motion stagger. Queued AFTER PB + lucky drop overlays via a tiny toast queue.
- Tier points: introduce QuestCompletion table tracking (userId, questId, completedAt). Each completion adds +0.5 to the user's tier score, capped at +20 lifetime. This is a controlled re-introduction of `tierScoreBonus` — the audit-trail (per-quest rows) means it's NOT a silent injection like the old lucky-drop bonus was. Need to surface it in the tier breakdown modal as 'Quest bonus: +12 score' so users see why their score shifted.
- Leaderboard weighting: since quest bonus feeds the canonical tier score, leaderboards automatically reflect it (no separate column needed). Cap of +20 means it can lift someone by 2 tier breakpoints max — meaningful but not game-breaking.

Slice plan:
1. Pool expansion (just append to QUEST_POOL + new isDone closures).
2. Per-user rotation (replace `pickTodayQuest()` signature to take userId + iso, hash both).
3. Completion persistence (Prisma table) + tier score injection capped at +20 with visibility in tier breakdown.
4. Celebration animation + queue ordering (use existing celebrate primitives).

Gates: needs design call on the tier-bonus cap (+20 lifetime) — same value as the removed lucky-drop bonus. Confirm with @maaiz before Slice 3.

They should have friends too and an add client option for their friends discreetly not too in the way'.

[2026-05-23] Slice 1 shipped (schema + endpoints, NO UI):
- New Friendship Prisma model added: { id, userAId, userBId, status: 'pending'|'accepted'|'blocked', requestedAt, acceptedAt }. Cascade-delete on both User sides. @@unique([userAId, userBId]). User got two new relations (friendshipsA / friendshipsB).
- Message.type now accepts 'friend_request' (no schema change — Message.type was already a free-form String). POST /api/friends auto-creates a Message of this type so the recipient sees a notification in the existing messages stream.
- New /api/friends route with all four verbs:
  - GET: returns { accepted, pendingSent, pendingReceived } buckets shaped from the viewer's POV (each row carries `friend: { id, username }` regardless of which side userA is).
  - POST { toUsername }: looks up the target user by username (case-sensitive — uses Prisma's unique lookup, matching how the rest of the app treats usernames), validates self-friend / dupe / blocked, creates a pending Friendship row + a 'friend_request' Message. Special case: if the target already has a PENDING request to me, POST auto-accepts (handshake symmetry).
  - PATCH { friendshipId, action: 'accept'|'decline'|'block' }: only the recipient can accept/decline; decline deletes the row; block can be called from either side and swaps userAId so the blocker always becomes userA.
  - DELETE { friendshipId }: unfriend (any side). Cannot delete a 'blocked' row — must PATCH to unblock first.
- All endpoints gated by the ironlog-uid cookie (same pattern as /api/trainer/request).

Current state: analytics ARE there but scattered — VolumeHeatmap on Dashboard, body-metric chart on Dashboard, EXERCISES tab has per-exercise progression sparkline (only for current-split exercises), tier sub-rank details inside the tier modal. Power-user-grade insights (e1RM trends per exercise, weekly volume regression slope, PR-rate-of-change) are computed inside computeAthleteTier but only surfaced as one-liners in the sub-rank detail strings.

Proposed:
1. New 'ANALYTICS' sub-tab on Progress (alongside Dashboard + Exercises). OR reorganise Dashboard to lead with the most useful charts at the top.
2. Charts to include (each with a 1-sentence plain-English interpretation underneath):
   - Per-exercise e1RM trendline. Powered by the same recentSetsByExercise + epley1RM that feeds the Strength sub-rank. Multi-line with up to 6 top lifts; tap a line to isolate.
   - Weekly volume heatmap (already exists on Dashboard — keep, but add month gridlines + trend annotation 'rising 1.2%/wk').
   - Body composition dual-axis chart: weight (left axis) + BF% (right axis) over time, with 90d-rolling mean overlay. Powered by BodyMetric rows.
   - Session-frequency calendar: monthly heat-grid showing days with at least one session. Surfaces consistency patterns + breaks.
   - PR rate-of-change: bar chart of PR count per month, last 6mo. Shows whether the user is still making progress or plateauing.
3. Interpretation footer per chart: pulls from the existing tier sub-rank detail strings (already computed by computeAthleteTier) so we don't re-derive — just re-surface them as 'what this chart tells you'.
4. De-gamify respect: charts always visible (analytics are educational, not gamification). Tier-overlay decorations (animal emojis, headline scores in chart corners) hidden in pure mode.

Slices:
1. New Progress sub-tab + reuse existing VolumeHeatmap + body-metric chart at the top with new framing copy.
2. Add per-exercise e1RM trendline (multi-line chart, top 6 lifts).
3. Add session-frequency calendar + PR rate-of-change.
4. Interpretation footers for each chart.

Gates: needs design call on whether ANALYTICS is a new sub-tab vs a Dashboard reorder. Recommended new sub-tab — keeps Dashboard scannable for the casual user, gives a dedicated home for serious power-users to dig in. Pairs with the dashboard-cards-rearrangeable planning item.

items.title: Admin migration — convert one-side-plates-only entries to total-on-bar
steps: Dry-run first: curl -X POST <host>/api/admin/migrate-bar-weights -H 'x-admin-key: $ADMIN_SECRET' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"maaiz","dryRun":true,"barbellBarKg":20,"ezCurlBarKg":7}'
Verify the response shows logsCount, logsToTouch, setsToMutate, and a sample[] array of {key, before, after, bar, date} — each `after` should equal `before*2 + bar`.
Verify the sample looks correct — bench press 60 → 140 (60*2+20), squat 60 → 140, EZ-curl 15 → 37 (15*2+7).
If satisfied, run again with dryRun:false to apply. Response includes appliedCount.
Check Vercel function logs for the audit line: [admin/migrate-bar-weights] target=@maaiz (...) logs-touched=N sets-mutated=M.

Open Maaiz's Progress dashboard — verify the strength PR table now shows realistic 'total on bar' weights, and the tier breakdown's Strength + Volume sub-ranks recompute (might tick up a tier or two).
items.notes:
[2026-05-23] Per @maaiz: 'All of maaiz input have been one side plates only for all barbell related exercises, and without bar weight. Can you update maaiz data for barbell or ez curl included weights? Always used the smaller ez curl bar'.

Built /api/admin/migrate-bar-weights as a re-runnable one-off endpoint:
- Header: x-admin-key (gated by ADMIN_SECRET env var)
- Body: { username, dryRun (default true), barbellBarKg (default 20), ezCurlBarKg (default 7) }
- Mutation formula: new_weight = current_weight * 2 + bar_kg
- Detection: every set whose exerciseId maps to an EXERCISES entry tagged with equipment:'barbell'. The id 'ez-bar-curl' (or any future id containing 'ez-bar') uses ezCurlBarKg; everything else uses barbellBarKg.
- Dry-run returns counts + first 20 mutations as a preview sample. Apply with dryRun:false.
- Vercel function log line on apply: [admin/migrate-bar-weights] target=... logs-touched=N sets-mutated=M.
- Reuses the same endpoint for any future user who reports the same convention drift — pass their username + custom bar weights if different.

Follow-up to consider: a per-user `inputConventionMigratedAt` flag so we don't double-apply. Currently safe to re-run since the formula doubles + adds bar, but if hit twice the second pass would inflate further. Until that flag lands, treat this endpoint as run-once-per-user.

Implementation:

- New helper `bestForNames(state, ['bench press'])` — returns the max kg across any exercise whose lowercased name contains the substring. Multi-name lists catch synonyms (e.g. ['overhead press', 'military press', 'shoulder press']).
- Substring matching deliberately loose so incline bench / decline bench / dumbbell bench all count toward the bench press benchmarks. Future option: restrict to barbell variants only if the user wants stricter benchmarks.

- Cardio: first / 10 / 50 sessions + 50 / 250 / 1000 km cumulative distance

Detection:

- Cardio session = any session containing at least one exercise with `type === 'cardio'`.

State wiring: MilestoneState gained `hiitSessionCount`, `cardioSessionCount`, `totalCardioMinutes`, `totalCardioKm`. Populated by the same history walker that computes maxByName + totalVolumeKg + warmup/cooldown flags.

items.title: Achievements unlock permanent tier-score additions (planning)
steps: (Planning — NO code shipped.) Verify each unlocked milestone in /ACHIEVEMENTS.md adds a small permanent number to the user's tier headline score (e.g. +0.5 to +2 per milestone, capped).

Verify trainer-specific milestones (in the trainer category of the achievements catalogue) ONLY contribute to the trainer-tier headline — NOT the athlete-tier headline. Athlete milestones contribute to the athlete headline.
Verify the boost is rendered as its own visible sub-rank line ('🏅 Achievements · X/100') in the tier breakdown so it's never a hidden buff (cf. the deprecated tierScoreBonus).
Verify boosts persist across sessions and survive logout/login (stored server-side, tied to MilestoneUnlock rows).
items.notes:
[2026-05-23] Per @maaiz: 'achievements/milestones contribute to the tiers right? Specifically trainer milestones for the trainer tier and they can be permanent tier additions by achievements unlocked'. Currently milestones (MILESTONES catalogue in lib/milestones.ts) unlock toasts + avatar grants but do NOT contribute to the tier score. Athlete tier is the average of 7 sub-ranks; trainer tier is the average of 5 sub-ranks. This planning item adds an 8th athlete sub-rank ('Achievements') and a 6th trainer sub-rank, each scored 0-100 based on the user's unlocked-milestone progress within the corresponding category.

Proposed:
- New ACHIEVEMENT_WEIGHTS table (small static map in lib/milestones.ts): each milestone id → { weight: number, ladder: 'athlete' | 'trainer' }. Weight is the milestone's contribution to a 0-100 score; sum of all athlete-ladder weights = 100, sum of all trainer-ladder weights = 100.
- New sub-rank computation: for the visitor, sum the weights of their unlocked milestones in each ladder. Cap at 100. Pass into computeAthleteTier (`achievementScore`) and computeTrainerTier (`achievementScore`).
- Each sub-rank gets a row in the modal: '🏅 Achievements · N/M unlocked · X/100'. Visible, labelled, NOT a hidden boost (cf. the deprecated tierScoreBonus principle).
- Permanent: once an achievement is unlocked it can never be lost, so the score is monotonically non-decreasing for that lever. (Other sub-ranks like Strength/Progression still trend up AND down with current behaviour.)
- Trainer-only milestones (achievements-v1 catalogue under category=Trainer) feed ONLY the trainer ladder. Athlete-only milestones feed ONLY the athlete ladder. Cross-role milestones (very few, e.g. account-age) feed BOTH at half weight.
- Surface in the modal under the existing sub-rank list with a small '↑ unlock more in Progress → Achievements' link.

Gates: needs achievements-v1 to ship first (planning lives in /ACHIEVEMENTS.md). When that lands, this becomes a 1-slice add-on: extend computeAthleteTier + computeTrainerTier signatures, wire the ACHIEVEMENT_WEIGHTS map, render the new sub-rank row.

Note: this is the closest thing to a 'pay-to-win' lever the app should have — but it's earned by IN-APP ACHIEVEMENTS, not money, and every contribution is visible + labelled.

items.title: Forced password reset flow
steps: Open admin panel → tap '🔒 FORCE RESET' for a test user.

Confirm the alert shows BOTH the TEMP password AND a '✓ flag verified true in DB' line. If the line reads '⚠ flag state in DB: false/null', the write silently failed — investigate Vercel logs and rerun.
Verify the temp password is on the clipboard (paste somewhere to check).

Already-logged-in case: have the same test user already signed in on another device/tab. Wait up to 60 seconds, or background and re-foreground the app. Verify they're bounced to the must-reset-password screen automatically — no manual log-out needed.
Fresh-login case: log in as the test user using the TEMP password — old password should no longer work. Verify you land on the must-reset-password screen, NOT the dashboard.
Tap the 👁 eye toggle next to each password field — verify it reveals/hides typed characters.
Enter a new password and confirm.
Verify you are then taken to the dashboard normally.
Confirm mustResetPassword is now false in the DB and the new password works on subsequent logins.
Server-side audit: check Vercel function logs for a line starting '[admin/force-reset]' with the target username, both flag values (write + reread), and timestamp.
items.notes:
[2026-05-23 hardening pass] Per @maaiz: 'Amaniis user was stuck on must reset password in admin panel, but she wasn't getting asked to set up a new password on next login attempt … take them to reset password immediately on next app open if still logged in, otherwise just prompt to make a new password on trying to log in with username'. Code review found the standard flow was wired correctly (login → mustReset → reset screen) but the in-session case had no refresh trigger — a logged-in user whose tab was foregrounded the whole time would never re-fetch /api/auth, so the admin's flag flip never propagated. Fixes:
- Client: refreshUser now fires on visibilitychange (existing) PLUS pageshow (iOS bfcache + PWA wake-up), window focus (desktop), AND a 60s background interval. Whichever fires first, the client picks up mustReset=true and renders the reset screen immediately on app reopen / focus.
- Server: /api/admin force-reset now re-reads the user row after the write and returns verifiedMustReset; also writes a server-side audit log via console.log (visible in Vercel function logs) tagged [admin/force-reset] with username, id, write-flag, reread-flag, ts. Confirms whether the write actually landed.
- Admin UI alert now quotes the verified-true / verified-false state alongside the temp password so the admin sees real DB state, not just optimistic local UI.
- Existing 'prompt on next username login' path unchanged — already worked, ships intact.
[2026-05-21] Fixed: admin force-reset now generates a TEMP password (via lib/crypto.generateTempPassword), hashes + saves it, AND flips mustResetPassword=true. The plaintext temp is returned to the admin UI (auto-copied to clipboard + shown in the alert) so they can share it with the user. Previously the action only flipped the flag without changing the password, so a user who'd forgotten their old password still couldn't log in — the must-reset prompt never had a chance to fire. (qa: Amanii: 'Admin panel says reset password required but can't log in because no prompt to put new password')
[2026-05-21 ecd2e59] Fixed: must-reset screen password fields declare autocomplete="new-password" so iCloud Keychain offers to update the saved credential when the user sets their new password.
[2026-05-21 01da6f1] Fixed: must-reset screen now has eye toggle on both password fields.

(Reported by @maaiz: 'Make user select what time weight was recorded morning or evening / advise weight should be recorded prior to workouts ideally in the morning / make weight recordings recognisable on the graph by color code'.)

items.title: Unlock Your Abs — gender-aware BF threshold + clearer 'to lose' wording + gender lock
steps: MALE user — open home. The mission card now reads: 🔓 'Unlock Your Abs · Drop your body fat to 15% or lower — that's where the six-pack reveals itself.' No deadline. Joining sets goal BF to 15%.

FEMALE user — open home. Card now reads: 🔓 'Unlock Your Abs · Drop your body fat to 22% or lower — that's where the six-pack reveals itself (women's essential fat is higher than men's, so this is calibrated for you).' No deadline. Joining sets goal BF to 22%.
OTHER / gender-not-set user — card uses the default 15% threshold + a note: '(we use a default threshold; set your gender in the profile for a tailored target)'.

Pre-join preview now reads: 'You're at 22.0% · lose 7.0% body fat to unlock (target 15%)' (was the ambiguous '7.0% to unlock' — @maaiz: 'make it clearer thats the amount to lose to complete the mission').
Joined view's foot row also surfaces the loss target: '22.0% → 15% (lose 7.0%)' on the left, % fill on the right.

Settings → Profile → GENDER. Once a gender is set, the buttons are locked with a 🔒 LOCKED chip + a footer note 'Gender is locked once set so body-composition missions + future gender-specific achievements stay consistent.' Server-side: POST /api/profile rejects gender mismatches on existing profiles with 'Gender is locked once set'.
If no body fat readings exist yet, JOIN is blocked + inline red error '⚠ Log a body fat reading first (Progress → Body)…'
Reload home — dismissal + join state persist (LocalStorage + milestone storage both hold them).
items.notes:
[2026-05-23] Slice 2 shipped: gender-aware threshold + 'to lose' wording + gender lock. Per @maaiz: (i) 'Unlock your abs said 10.7% to unlock - make it clearer thats the amount to lose to complete the mission'; (ii) 'the amount for unlock your abs probably different for men and women'; (iii) 'check and make sure they cant change their gender after initial selection'.

Changes:
- lib/challenges.ts: Mission.targetByGender?: { male: number; female: number } added. New helpers resolveMissionTarget(m, gender) and resolveMissionBody(m, gender) — the latter substitutes the per-gender target into the body copy and appends a note explaining the calibration.
- mission-unlock-abs-v1: targetByGender = { male: 15, female: 22 }. Default target=15 (used for 'other' / unknown gender).
- app/page.tsx ChallengesCard now takes a `gender` prop (threaded from `ob.gender`). All UI sites use the resolved target — preview text, progress bar denominator, profile goal PATCH, joined-view headline + foot row.
- Wording: preview now reads 'lose X.X% body fat to unlock (target Y%)' (was 'X.X% to unlock'). Joined view foot reads 'cur% → target% (lose X.X%)'.
- Gender lock: Settings → Profile → GENDER buttons now disabled + greyed out when ob.gender is already set; ARIA disabled + cursor-not-allowed; footer note explains why. Server-side: POST /api/profile rejects with 400 'Gender is locked once set — contact support to change.' when existing profile.gender exists and request gender differs.
[2026-05-22] Shipped: new MISSIONS array in lib/challenges.ts (open-ended, no time cap). mission-unlock-abs-v1: body_fat_at_or_below 15%, setsProfileGoal=true. On JOIN: PATCH /api/profile sets targetBodyFatPct=15. JOIN blocked + inline error if user has no BF reading. New milestone 'abs-unlocked' triggers on logBodyMetric when bodyFatPct <= 15 — pipeline reads MILESTONE_STORAGE_KEY, pushes onto setMilestoneQueue so the celebration overlay fires. MissionState 'achieved' is sticky (won't unflip on a regression reading) AND fires immediately if user is already at or below target at any reading. bodyMetrics now eagerly-fetched on user mount so home Mission card has live data even before user visits Body tab. (Reported by @maaiz: 'Make a 6 month challenge for body fat under 15% and call it something about unlocking abs' → revised to 'Actually no need for a 6 month time limit / Can just be a challenge anyone joins and it should automatically update their goal body fat but show an error if they haven't recorded any / It can also be a milestone unlock if someone has or achieves under the abs %'.)

items.title: Scoring rewards rest days + caps overtraining
steps: Set profile.daysPerWeek to 4. Train EXACTLY 4 distinct days a week for 4 weeks. Open Progress → Dashboard and confirm your Consistency sub-rank reads high (~85+) — the adherence dimension is at 100%.

Same user, train 7 days/week for 4 weeks (overtrain). Verify Consistency DROPS — adherence is now ~150% which the curve scores around 25-50 points. Detail line should read '... (over target — rest!)'.
Train 0 days for 4 weeks. Verify Consistency drops to whatever lifetime-sessions alone scores (~40-50% of previous if you had a year of training).
Verify the streak component still exists but is heavily de-weighted (10% of consistency) — a 14-day streak alone won't max consistency anymore.
Verify the Volume sub-rank is unchanged in its formula (still log curve to 100k kg-reps midpoint) — going harder still earns volume points, but the headline is dragged by consistency adherence.
Switch profile.daysPerWeek to 6 → adherence target rescales to 24 sessions in 4 weeks. Verify the detail line updates.
items.notes: [2026-05-22] Shipped: replaced 0.6*sessions + 0.4*streak with 0.5*sessions + 0.4*adherence + 0.1*streak in the consistency sub-rank. Adherence peaks at 100% of weekly target (daysPerWeek * 4 over 4 weeks) and DROPS past that: 150% scores 50, 200% scores 0. Rest days now FEED the score by leaving the user closer to target. Server-side stats compute sessionsLast4Weeks (distinct days) + fetches daysPerWeek from UserProfile to pipe into computeAthleteTier; client memo does the same. (Reported by @maaiz: 'Points should be fair to reward sufficient rest days and minimise reward for going too hard'.)

items.title: Global tier leaderboard (cross-app ranking)
steps: Open the tier explainer modal (tap your tier chip on home). Verify a new 🌍 GLOBAL TIER LEADERBOARD button below the JUMP TO MY ROW button.
Tap it → standalone 'GLOBAL · TIER LEADERBOARD' view opens with two tabs (🏆 ATHLETES / 🤝 TRAINERS) and three lenses (TOP 100 / YOUR TIER / AROUND YOU).
Athlete tab + TOP 100 shows up to 100 ranked rows. Rows of users who opted out of public visibility render as 'Athlete #<rank>'; everyone else shows @username. Your own row reads 'YOU' regardless.
Trainer tab works the same but ALL trainer rows show @username (no anonymous toggle for trainers — public for client discovery).
YOUR TIER lens filters to only your tier number (e.g. all Tier 4s).
AROUND YOU lens centers your row with 5 above + 5 below.
Meta strip shows total ranked + your rank + your tier badge.
Open Settings → APP PREFERENCES → 🌍 GLOBAL BOARD toggle. Flip it ON. Reload the global view → verify your row shows as 'Athlete #<rank>' (except 'YOU' on your own viewer).
items.notes: [2026-05-22] Shipped: GET /api/leaderboard/global?kind=athlete|trainer&lens=top|band|around. Athletes ranked by computeStatsForUsers tier score; min 5 sessions to qualify (bots + casual filter). Trainers ranked by computeTrainerTier breakdown (5-dim including Discipline). Schema field UserProfile.hideFromGlobalLeaderboard (default false) lets athletes opt out; trainers can't (per user direction). Standalone view GlobalLeaderboardView in app/page.tsx with kind/lens tabs + meta header. Wired from TierInfoModal via a new onOpenGlobalLeaderboard callback. Settings toggle added in APP PREFERENCES, hidden for trainers. (Reported by @maaiz: 'Is there a tier global leaderboard anywhere? Should we have it?')

items.title: Trainer tier includes Discipline sub-rank (own athlete score)
steps: As a trainer with at least one client, open the tier explainer modal (tap your tier chip on home). Verify the 🎯 YOUR TRAINER SUB-RANKS panel now shows FIVE bars (was 4): Roster, Progression, Retention, Reach, AND Discipline (🏋 icon).

Discipline detail line should read 'Your own athlete score · N/100' where N matches your headline athlete score on Progress → Dashboard. If you're slacking on your personal training, this number is low.
Path-to-next callout should correctly identify Discipline as the lowest sub-rank if it is the lowest.

Headline tier score is now the AVG of 5 sub-ranks (was 4). Expect existing trainer tiers to drop by ~10-15 points overall — that's intentional: a trainer who never trains themselves shouldn't sit at Pro/Elite.
Train yourself (log sessions, set PRs) and refresh — verify your trainer headline ticks UP as your athlete score climbs.
Edge case: brand-new trainer with 0 clients should still see Discipline as a meaningful dimension — if their own athlete score is e.g. 40, their trainer headline should be ≥ ~8 (40/5).
items.notes: [2026-05-22] Shipped: added selfAthleteScore to TrainerStatsForTier; new Discipline sub-rank in computeTrainerTier averaging into the headline. Server endpoint /api/trainer/me/tier now also fetches the trainer's own computeStatsForUsers([uid]) result and passes the canonical score in. Trainer tier surfaces (modal, Settings IDENTITY, leaderboard) all read the same 5-dim breakdown. (Reported by @maaiz: 'I want the athlete tier a trainer has to play a role in the trainer tier — they can't be slacking and be a good trainer'.)

items.title: Trainers see their athlete tier on Progress dashboard too
steps: Log in as a TRAINER (or admin with the trainer extra-role)
Open Progress → Dashboard tab
Verify the athlete tier card now appears (previously hidden because the gate was role === 'user'). Shows the headline animal tier + 5 sub-rank bars + experience badge + 'path to next' callout
Verify the card reflects the trainer's OWN training history — their own sessions / PRs / volume / mastery / habits — not their clients'
Verify other role-specific cards (e.g. trainer-only client roster cards in the trainer section) still appear correctly elsewhere
Toggle Pure Mode ON — verify the athlete tier card hides for the trainer too (same de-gamify treatment)

Open the tier explainer modal (tap your tier chip on home). Verify a new 🎯 YOUR TRAINER SUB-RANKS panel appears below the trainer ladder with 4 bars (Roster / Progression / Retention / Reach), each showing N/100 score + a short detail line. Verify a 'Path to next' callout points at the lowest sub-rank.
items.notes:
[2026-05-22] Shipped server-side multi-dim trainer tier: new GET /api/trainer/me/tier endpoint computes the full TierBreakdown via computeTrainerTier() from the trainer's roster stats (rosterCount, clientsWithRecentPR, clientsWithActiveStreak, totalClientPRs, totalClientVolumeKg). HomePage fetches it on mount, passes through HomeGlobals → TierInfoModal as `trainerBreakdown`. Modal renders the 4 sub-rank bars + Path-to-Next callout when the breakdown is present, and the headline tier in the trainer ladder ribbon now sources from the breakdown (with getTrainerTier(clients.length) as fallback during loading).
[2026-05-21] Removed the `role === 'user'` gate from the athlete tier card so trainers and admins get to see their personal training rank alongside whatever role-specific surfaces they have. Trainers also train; rewarding them for it makes the app feel less like 'two separate apps'. Card is still hidden in Pure Mode for users who opt out of gamification.

items.title: Per-step comments on /qa items
steps: Open /qa, expand any item with multiple steps in its `steps[]` array (e.g. workout-set-logging).
Verify each step now has a small 💬 button on the right. Steps that have existing comments scoped to them show the count next to the icon (e.g. 💬 2).
Tap the 💬 button on step 3 — verify the page scrolls to the comment form, the form shows a '💬 STEP 3' indicator chip at the top, and the indicator has a '× CLEAR' button.
Type a note, pick a status, tap save. Verify the new comment renders in the thread with a small '💬 STEP 3' chip next to the tester name + timestamp.
Tap '× CLEAR' on the indicator before saving another comment — verify the next comment saves WITHOUT a step scope (legacy item-level behaviour).
Refresh the page — verify the step counts on the 💬 buttons stay accurate (read from the comments thread), and the per-step chips on saved comments persist.
items.notes: [2026-05-22] Slice 1 shipped: schema (QAComment.stepIndex Int?), POST /api/qa/comment accepts + validates stepIndex (0-99), GET returns it, /qa UI renders 💬 buttons per step + comment-form indicator + per-comment chip in the thread. Slice 2 (analytics: group thread by step in the admin view, filter all comments by step) deferred.

items.title: Milestone info overlay — tap a badge to see unlock criteria or earned details
steps: Open Settings → tap 🏆 ACHIEVEMENTS to expand the wall

Tap a LOCKED (greyed-out) milestone tile — verify an info overlay opens with: greyscale icon, '🔒 LOCKED · CATEGORY' header, milestone label, a 'HOW TO UNLOCK' card containing the plain-English requirement (e.g. 'Complete 10 lifetime sessions' or 'Train at least once a day for 7 consecutive days'), and a 'TAP ANYWHERE TO CLOSE' hint

Tap the backdrop or the ✕ button — verify the overlay closes

Verify every milestone in MILESTONES (lib/milestones.ts) now has a 'requirement' string — check at least 5 different categories (anniversary, consistency, strength, behaviour, tier) display the right unlock text

Modal styled differently for earned vs locked (gold vs grey border, ✓ ACHIEVED vs 🔒 LOCKED header, body vs requirement card). items.title: Training principles knowledge base (lib/principles.ts)

Verify lib/experience.ts experienceProfile() pulls deloadWindowWeeks from DELOAD_POLICY in principles.ts (newcomer 8w, beginner 6w, intermediate 5w, advanced 4w)
Verify lib/performance.ts suggestProgression() has a header comment referencing the principle file's RPE scale

items.title: Progress photo log via Vercel Blob

items.title: Offline-tolerant workout save with replay queue
steps: Turn off Wi-Fi + mobile data on the device
Start a workout and finish it. Verify the session saves locally without throwing an error
Open home — verify a yellow '☁ 1 PENDING' chip appears next to the YOUR SPLIT row
Reconnect to network — verify within a couple of seconds the chip disappears and the session is now in the server history (reload to confirm)
Test queueing multiple offline saves: finish two sessions while offline, verify the chip reads '☁ 2 PENDING'
Stress test: kill the network mid-save (not before). Verify the session still queues
Verify a queued item is dropped after 5 failed replay attempts to avoid permanent stuck state
items.notes: [2026-05-21] lib/offlineSync.ts. postWithQueue() attempts the network POST, stashes in localStorage on failure (or skips network if navigator.onLine === false). drainQueue() replays on 'online' event; on mount if already online; after each session save. queueCount() drives a '☁ N PENDING' chip in the home view header. Items max 5 replay attempts before drop to prevent permanent stuck state. Currently wired into /api/workout POST only; other saves can opt in later.

items.title: Daily Quest + Full-Stack Day combo + Balanced Week + Hidden achievements

Hit the quest's condition (e.g. log 8 glasses for 💧 Hydrate) — verify the card turns green with '✓ QUEST COMPLETE'
Different day — verify a different quest may appear (the per-date hash picks one of 7 quests)

Hit 30 days of hydration target → verify 💎 30-Day Hydra hidden achievement fires
Complete 7 lifetime Full Stack Days (hydration + sleep + energy + session in the same day) → verify 🏛 Full Stack × 7 fires

items.title: De-gamify toggle in Settings (Pure Mode)

items.title: Habits sub-rank — hydration + sleep + energy feed the tier

items.title: Wellness card — hydration / sleep / energy / soreness / injuries
steps: Open Progress → Dashboard. Verify a '🌱 WELLNESS' collapsed card sits at the top with a one-line summary (💧 0/8 · 😴 -h · ⚡ -/5 · 💢 N · 🤕 N)
Expand it. Verify four sections appear:

items.title: Tier scoring v2 — e1RM trend, Progression, Body Comp (sex-aware), hasData weighting
steps: Open Progress (athlete dashboard) → tap your tier chip. Modal lists 7 sub-ranks: Consistency, Strength, Progression, Volume, Mastery, Body Comp, Habits.

Verify Strength's detail line reads `<+/-X.X>% e1RM (180d, top N)` instead of `<n> personal bests`. New users with <4 sets logged on any exercise see `log ≥4 sets of an exercise to start tracking` and the sub-rank is excluded from the headline (hasData=false).
Verify Progression's detail line reads `<+/-X.X>%/wk volume trend · Nwk`. Users with <9 weeks of training history see `log N more weeks to unlock progression` and the sub-rank is excluded.

Verify Body Comp's detail line shows BF% and/or weight plus `· ♂ curve` or `· ♀ curve` based on UserProfile.gender. Users with neither weight nor BF logged see `log weight or body-fat to track condition` (excluded from headline). Female users with the same fitness as a male should NOT score systematically lower.

Verify Consistency's detail reads `<n>/<target> last 4wk · streak <m>wk` — the streak is now WEEKLY (consecutive weeks hitting daysPerWeek target), not daily. Training 4/wk perfectly when daysPerWeek=4 should grow the weekly streak each week even with rest days in between.
Verify Mastery's detail reads `<n> exercises ≥4 sets (last 6mo) · <m> lifetime`. Exercises logged once or twice in 6 months should NOT count toward the count.

Verify headline tier feels right for a 1-month newbie (Tier 1-2), a 6-month grinder (Tier 3-4), and a 2-year veteran (Tier 4-5). No-one should be pinned at the bottom because they don't log body comp / wellness — those sub-ranks drop out via hasData.
Verify `tierScoreBonus` (the lucky-drop bonus shown on the avatar page) NO LONGER adds to the canonical tier score — the headline is now pure f(stats).

Verify per-set RPE contributes to IP: log a set with RPE 10 → +3 IP, RPE 9 → +2 IP, RPE 8 → +1 IP, RPE ≤7 → 0 IP. Summed across all sets, the IP shown on the client leaderboard reflects (stored superset/dropset awards) + (per-set RPE bonus).
Verify `Path to next` callout now points at the sub-rank with the LARGEST score-upside-to-100, not just the lowest absolute score (so a 49 Volume beats a 30 Habits as the suggested focus area).
items.notes:
[2026-05-23 <sha7>] Slice 1/1 (FULL ROLLOUT): shipped all 9 items from the design plan. Reworked lib/tiers.ts with new sub-ranks (Strength=e1RM trend, Progression=weekly volume regression, Body Comp=sex-aware current+90d-maintenance). Consistency rebuilt: 30% 180d-sessions + 60% adherence + 10% weekly streak (dropped lifetime totalSessions, dropped daily streak). Mastery filter raised to ≥4 sets in 180d. tierScoreBonus removed from headline math (still awarded to profile field for the lucky-drop UX, just not blended). hasData flag per sub-rank → headline averages only over dims with signal. focusNext picks highest 100-score upside. lib/leaderboardStats.ts now reads UserProfile.gender, computes per-exercise sets / weekly volumes / 90d body deltas / RPE bonus IP. computeStatsFromLogs backward-compat preserved.

items.notes:

items.title: Trainers can author missions for their clients (planning)
steps: (Planning — NO code shipped.) Verify trainers see a '+ NEW MISSION' button in their Settings → TRAINING section.

Verify mission authoring form: title, body, metric type (body_fat_at_or_below | body_weight_at_or_below | total_volume_kg | total_sessions), target, optional duration, scope picker (all my clients | specific group | specific clients).

items.notes:
[2026-05-23] Question from @maaiz: 'missions i guess get added as trainers make them as well?' followed by 'missions can be set for groups too right? not just clients individually'. Answer to both: yes — group scope folded into the scope picker. Design needed before code. Current state: MISSIONS array in lib/challenges.ts is a hardcoded catalogue (only 'Unlock Your Abs' for now). To let trainers author missions:

Proposed model:
- New `Mission` Prisma model { id, createdBy (userId of trainer), scope ('my-clients' | 'group' | 'specific'), groupId? (set when scope='group'), title, body, icon, metric, target, durationDays?, setsProfileGoal, targetByGender, createdAt, updatedAt }.
- New `MissionAssignment` if scope='specific' { missionId, clientId } so trainers can hand-pick clients per mission.
- API: POST /api/trainer/missions (create), GET /api/missions (returns built-ins + missions visible to current user), PATCH /api/trainer/missions/:id (edit), DELETE.
- Visibility: a mission is visible to user X if (a) it's built-in, OR (b) X is a client of the createdBy trainer AND scope='my-clients', OR (c) scope='group' AND X is a member of the referenced LeaderboardGroup, OR (d) scope='specific' AND X is in the MissionAssignment list.
- UI: Settings → TRAINING gets a '+ NEW MISSION' button (trainer-only). Mission authoring form with scope picker: ALL MY CLIENTS / SPECIFIC GROUP (picks one of their LeaderboardGroups) / SPECIFIC CLIENTS (multi-select). Athletes see the merged catalogue in the existing MISSIONS section.
- 'Global' scope intentionally NOT in v1 — would let any trainer broadcast to the entire app which needs moderation. Admin-curated global missions stay as the built-in catalogue.

Slices:
1. Schema (Mission + MissionAssignment) + POST/GET endpoints + admin/trainer creation form with my-clients scope only.
2. Group scope — extend create form with group picker; visibility query joins LeaderboardGroupMember.
3. Specific-clients scope (MissionAssignment) — multi-select picker; visibility joins MissionAssignment.
4. Edit / delete UI.

Gates: needs design call on whether mission-bonus quest score (planned future work) should accept trainer-authored missions, or only built-ins.

items.notes:
[2026-06-05 <sha7>] ROOT CAUSE FOUND + fixed (qa: trainer-request-pending-state). The desync the round-3 note suspected is real and it is HISTORICAL: a TrainerRequest can be status='accepted' with NO TrainerClient row. The current accept PATCH is already atomic, but (a) pre-2026-05-24 accepts ran the insert AFTER committing the status update, so a failed insert left 'accepted' with no roster row, and (b) even today a blind trainerClient.create() throws on the GLOBAL clientId @unique whenever the athlete already has any trainer row, and inside $transaction that throw rolls back the status update too. Every prior pass only patched CACHING — it never created the missing row, so cache-busting could never fix it. Three-part fix: (1) accept PATCH now upserts TrainerClient on the unique clientId (reassign to the accepting trainer) instead of create() — idempotent, never rolls back the accept; (2) GET /api/trainer/clients self-heals: before reading, it backfills TrainerClient rows for any accepted request of this trainer that has no row, via createMany+skipDuplicates (honours clientId unique so a client rostered to another trainer is left alone — fills gaps, never steals); (3) disown DELETE now also deletes the TrainerRequest so 'accepted request ⟺ rostered client' is a hard invariant and the backfill can't resurrect a disowned client. Amanii appears on the trainer's next Clients-hub load with zero user action. Retest: as a trainer, have a user accept your request, confirm they appear in CLIENTS; disown them, confirm they leave AND stay gone after refresh; re-adopt, confirm they come back.\n\n[2026-06-03 <sha7>] @maaiz cmpsoi8a20000jsm57z199ntq round 3 — same Amanii visibility issue STILL surfacing in the search results vs client list mismatch ('When I search Amanii I can see she accepted my client request but I can't see her in my client list'). Two separate code paths converge here: (a) the trainer search at /api/trainer/search reads from TrainerRequest + User tables directly and shows her with the 'accepted' status, (b) the Clients hub reads from /api/trainer/clients which joins via TrainerClient table — if her TrainerClient row exists but the GET response is stale, she's invisible. Mitigations from prior pass (cache-bust + window-focus refresh) addressed the cache angle. Outstanding investigation needed: confirm the PATCH /api/trainer/request handler is atomically creating BOTH the TrainerRequest.status update AND the TrainerClient insert in the same transaction — if the order is request-update-then-client-insert and the second fails silently, the search sees 'accepted' while the roster has nothing. Companion shipped: ✕ DISOWN CLIENT action in the profile preview modal (qa: trainer-disown-client-modal) so trainers can manage the relationship from the search/leaderboard/chat entry points once she IS visible. Slice 1/N; next slice: drop the response in a structured log when the TrainerClient insert path fires AND fails, plus add a maintenance endpoint that backfills missing TrainerClient rows from accepted TrainerRequests (admin-only).\n\n[2026-05-26] Recurring: Amanii reported accepted but not visible in client list. Likely root cause: cached /api/trainer/clients response (SW or browser). Three reinforcements: (a) GET route now sets Cache-Control: no-store + dynamic='force-dynamic' + revalidate=0, (b) frontend fetch uses cache:'no-store' + ?ts=Date.now() cache-bust query param, (c) new window-focus + visibilitychange handler force-refreshes the clients list whenever the trainer reopens the app from background. Existing view==='clientsHub' refresh kept. Per @maaiz 2026-05-26 'Says Amanii accepted my client request but don't see her on the client list'.

[2026-05-26] @maaiz retest re:l1dhjm6j: 'Not sure if push notification working, just checked if Amanii accepted my request and she did but not showing under my clients'. Two separate concerns: (a) push delivery uncertain, (b) accepted trainer-request not surfacing in CLIENTS hub. Investigate /api/trainer/clients return path + the post-accept hook. (qa: trainer-request-pending-state, trainer-client-auto-friend)

[2026-05-24] Shipped: /api/messages/[userId] joins TrainerRequest + Friendship status onto each request-typed message and returns it as requestStatus. Client renders a coloured chip on both sides. PATCH /api/trainer/request drops an in-app adoption_accepted / adoption_declined Message so the trainer aside reflects the outcome without push delivery.

items.title: Athlete tier headline is identical on Home, Progress dashboard, and the Rankings leaderboard (single source of truth)
steps: Open Home — read the athlete tier headline (e.g. BIG DAWG · T4).

items.notes:
[2026-05-26] Slice 1: Progress dashboard was building its OWN stripped stats object (missing weeklyVolumes, recentSetsByExercise, weight/bf, gender, intensityPoints, setsByMuscleGroup, daysPerWeek). Refactored to reuse the canonical `myAthleteBreakdown` useMemo from line 8287. Source: @maaiz screenshot — Home: BIG DAWG · T4, Progress: FOX · TIER 5 OF 6.

[2026-05-26 <sha7>] Slice 2: even after Slice 1 unified Home and Progress against the same local useMemo, both still disagreed with the LEADERBOARD when the score sat at a tier boundary. Leaderboard re-pulls fresh logs + bodyMetrics from the DB; the local useMemo runs off cached React state (history, bodyMetrics) which is one workout / one BF reading behind during the async data arrival window. New endpoint `GET /api/me/tier` returns the canonical CanonicalTier from the same `computeStatsForUsers` pipeline the leaderboard uses. Frontend fetches it on user load + on every history-total / bodyMetrics-count change. The `myAthleteBreakdown` useMemo now overlays this server-canonical headline onto the local breakdown (sub-ranks stay local so tile detail strings still match what's on screen). Result: home rail, progress YOUR RANK card, and leaderboard 'YOU' row all read the same tier label, tierNum, and headline score. Source: @maaiz screenshot 2026-05-26 'Got the achievement celebration or tier celebration for reaching lion on app open but it says big dawg on home and progress page. Which is it!?!?'.
